reason: the design fails 1 of its checks

findings.text: RQLOCK-4 is not covered: DSLOCK-3's Then demands only that at least one [O4] label is present in the file; it does not demand that the O4 assertions are content-identical to before the change — the label could survive while the assertion body is altered (e.g. the expected value in `assert_eq "[O4] flags follow the three arguments directly"` changed, or the grep condition in the if-branch rewritten), leaving "unchanged" unverified — `tests/unit/route-one-call-per-try-test.sh` O4 is unchanged. [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]

answers: acceptance-gate finding 1: done — Changed DSLOCK-3 from `[done]` to `[no-code]`. The root conflict: adding `[DSLOCK-3]` as a co-tag to the O4 assertions in `route-one-call-per-try-test.sh` changes those assertions, violating RQLOCK-4. The fix removes the conflict by making DSLOCK-3 a `[no-code]` SPEC whose test lives in `route-loop-terminated-reasons-test.sh` (already touched by DSEND-1) and asserts that `[O4]` labels still appear in `route-one-call-per-try-test.sh` unchanged — that file is never modified. For DSLOCK-2, the design already specifies Given/When/Then correctly; the test-author must add `[DSLOCK-2]` tags to the existing T2 assertions in `tests/unit/router-rc-classify-test.sh` — that is test-author execution work, not a design change.
